scope: Oracle exploratory screening; no router acceptance or claim of a fixed tail regression

screen-01.scope: R135 complete Oracle exploratory screen; CPU pairs kept separate
limitations: No router performance, statistical significance, equivalence or causal attribution is claimed. Oracle ranking is a screen only.
All four per-block observations are retained. Contrasts match the same block, CPU pair, affinity and lane; two CPU pairs are not pooled into eight independent same-core observations.
Absolute median paired change <= 1% is exploratory unresolved. Larger changes are descriptive lower/higher directions, not acceptance or rejection decisions; sign counts are reported separately.
Two workers, when present, run concurrently and share host resources. Affinity conditions and lanes share a subject daemon within a block; they are not independent daemon repetitions.
Boundary last_processor observations do not count migrations. Context-switch deltas cover the snapshot bracket, including measurement bookkeeping; they do not locate individual slow operations.
register_1/register_16 include ADD plus REMOVE; event_1 includes registration-generated object events, not a user SEND event workload.

Hash consistency is checked against the captured manifest; runner assertions establish live binary/library identities and cleanup. This report does not independently rehash Oracle binaries or recreate that environment.

syscalls.scope: Oracle structural syscall diagnostic only; all traced latency and CPU are excluded from performance claims.
syscalls.attribution: A successful recvmsg request prefix starts its phase. EAGAIN probes and epoll waits are assigned to the previously received request until the next successful request recvmsg. Startup precedes successful accept; connection setup, preflight, warmup, validation LOOKUPs and EOF teardown are separate from measured cycles. This is a prior-request convention, not a synchronized timed interval: the wait leading into the first measured request belongs to the prior warmup request, and the wait leading into the final LOOKUP belongs to the last measured request. epoll_wait and epoll_pwait are counted separately as printed by strace. Totals cover selected syscall families only, not every daemon syscall.
